P1.evidence: Warm open and a glancing setter reference — "kim tells me you've you're on a on a journey huh" — but nothing was actually read back. The four-part frame was never set and no frame agreement was sought; the call went straight from Texas small talk into the prospect's story. The opening question arrived only as "What's kind of had you looking at the kettlebell?" at 00:04:18, a product-first variant of the scripted open.

P2.evidence: Weight was asked directly — "How much do you weigh right now?" — and answered (165 lb, from 245 lb). Age and height were never asked. No health-conditions question was ever put: the diabetes, cholesterol and blood pressure history was volunteered in the first two minutes. No injury or limitation question either — the shoulder and joint inflammation was volunteered at 00:06 and the rep built a pitch on it without ever asking how long or how bad. Training week was properly established ("were you working out through the whole duration of those seven years?" leading to the full Mon/Wed/Fri picture). Diet was discussed but coached rather than asked ("if you're going to be doing keto, try to still include... more micronutrients"). Sleep never asked — the prospect raised it himself at 00:26 ("it'd be nice to get maybe another hour of sleep"). Energy never asked.

P3.evidence: The 7/10 scaling question was the best-run move of the call: "let's say the best peak version of you... is a 10 out of 10, where would you put yourself now?" followed by "What does a 10 look like? What is it that you really want?" — which produced the real goal. The reflect-back was clean and confirmed: "the thing that's bugging you is what you see in the reflection of the mirror doesn't represent the progress you've made" — "Yeah, 100%. 100%." But the call never went past the individual. "Who else does that impact?" was never asked, and the family material that would have carried the close — a wife who lost 100 lb alongside him, a son who needs conditioning to be allowed to play football — only surfaced at 00:37, after the commitment, as small talk. The rep even had the line and used it too late: "in six months, you'll be superhero dad."

P4.evidence: The past-attempts history arrived unprompted as narrative — Virta Health, calisthenics, dumbbells, the leaner-protein experiment that gave "mixed results". The rep never asked why anything stalled, never asked what the one thing in the way was, and never let the prospect name the gap. The prospect named it himself at 00:26, after the pitch and unprompted: "the biggest thing for me would be being held accountable for like the intensity and progress... I know my intensity could be probably better." Per the scoring rule that is a miss, not a hit — the script credits asking. This was the single most sellable admission on the call and the rep did not elicit it or build on it.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form. No two-year question, no 'willing to settle', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep went from the reflect-back straight to "if you feel like you're ready, I can walk you through what the coaching looks like" at 00:18. With no cost of inaction established, when the payment friction arrived twelve minutes later there was nothing to hold the urgency, and the rep filled the gap by cutting the deposit instead.

P6.evidence: The belief question was asked and answered — "do you feel like this can get you to where you want to be? that's the most important thing" — "yeah i think so". But it came at 00:25, after the full programme walk-through and the guarantee, not before presenting. The all-in question came later still and only as a gate on scheduling: "Is this something that you're definitely 100% all in on?" — "Yeah, for sure." The sequence is inverted: the rep presented first and checked commitment afterwards.

P11.evidence: Step 2 was the only step completed: the Trevor onboarding call was booked live for Monday 12:15 Central and the invite confirmed on the call. No payment was collected and no payment link was sent — the ask was reduced to $1,200 and then deferred entirely to a 2pm callback. No agreement email, nothing signed on the call, and no mention at all of the welcome email, the Skool community link or the onboarding questionnaire. The prospect was left holding a booked coaching slot he had not paid for, and said so himself: "I don't want to commit to him or have him commit to a timeframe without having paid him of course."

objection_plays.detail: "I wasn't expecting quite that big of a chunk, but I would have to make some arrangements like banking wise in order to process that payment." Almost none of the play ran. No isolate ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%') at the moment it landed — the all-in question came later and was aimed at scheduling, not at isolating. No 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'. No open-wallet permission question, and no financial picture whatsoever: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments. Instead the rep skipped straight to shrinking the ask — "we can just take a smaller down payment to still get everything going... we just need 1,200" — which is the one move the play is designed to prevent.

Script gap worth logging. The blocker here was not capacity to pay or willingness — the prospect said yes and stayed yes — it was same-day liquidity: funds sitting somewhere that required a physical bank visit to move. The playbook's money play assumes reluctance and probes for hidden capacity; it has no path for a committed buyer with a mechanical settlement delay. Absent that path the rep improvised a $1,200 deposit with no documented terms and released the onboarding slot unpaid. A scripted 'committed but cannot settle today' procedure — link sent live, deposit amount fixed by policy, onboarding held only on receipt — would have closed this cleanly.

notes: Excellent scaling question and reflect-back, then the whole spine of the process was skipped: no root cause asked, no consequence frame at all, commitment checked after presenting rather than before. The result is a call that produced a genuine verbal yes with nothing underneath it, and when cash friction appeared the rep discounted the entry point instead of running the money play. Coach two things: elicit the accountability gap rather than waiting for it, and never reduce the ask before the financial picture has been taken.
